answer: Proof of personhood protocols resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to mirror biometric data against a verified registry. This creates a hard cost, as generating fake identities requires bypassing liveness checks, pushing the system away from a security nadir. If an attacker attempts to flood the network with clones, the protocol triggers a violet alert to slash stake, forcing a high capital expenditure that renders mass identity fabrication economically irrational for any malicious actor.
